rh.number_traceability.prose_claims_cons.reason:
The printed numbers are correct. However, several prose claims about which fits are best, or where observed values fall, are contradicted by the logs and tables the paper itself contains.
(a) L766-768 says 'the best model in this entire study is an isotropic compressive scaling of an additive metric on CIE LCh coordinates'. The code only takes the best of the chord-coordinate isotropic fits (isotropic LCh, -1.822). The paper's own appendix panel and extra_cis.json show higher held-out log-likelihood for chromatic-arc M3 cone-opponent (-1.722), M3 LCh (-1.756) and M2 (-1.781), joint-arc M3 cone-opponent (-1.686) and joint-chord M3 LCh (-1.795). The arc version of the isotropy diagnostic, referenced only by pointer, also contradicts the Conclusion's claim (L909-913) that perceptual spaces are separated from cone space by a better isotropic metric: in arc coordinates CIELAB's isotropic metric is significantly worse than the cone one and LCh's is equal. (b) L619 says the observed coarse values '+0.079 and -0.184 ... fall ... inside the non-cone one'. Under the K2-CIELAB generator the logged K2-M1 range is [-0.106,+0.019], which excludes +0.079.

These are material contradictions between prose summaries and the underlying results.

rh.test_set_integrity.bootstrap_from_tra.reason: Every bootstrap that refits a model draws only from the training fold. The shape bootstrap resamples training-fold clusters and gives test units zero weight. The gray replication bootstrap draws from the training split's counts and scores on the held-out 50 responses per triad.
